proven: An administrator can create approved compute and storage plans in the instance-declared provider/region/billing profile; a request naming a different provider capability version is refused rather than stored.
A price policy version binds an exact approved compute/storage plan pair to one-month amounts; a missing pair or a non-approved plan is refused and no fallback rate exists.

Refund and retention policy versions are recorded with the frozen workspace-delete-refund-v1 algorithm and the 15-day/retain retention facts; a refund version referencing an unknown retention version is refused.

The single availability projection maps revoked/deprecated status to retired, an approved plan outside its validity window to unavailable, and refuses to store a request whose requested projection it cannot express.
A new price policy version and its catalog.policy_changed.v1 Outbox row plus one delivery row per contract-declared consumer (ledger, workspace) commit in one transaction.
Idempotent commands replay the original stored response for the same key and input, and refuse a reused key with different input.
notProven: No quote exists yet: CreateQuote/GetQuote/AcceptQuote are W15 and remain unimplemented, so the catalog cannot yet price a deploy/resize/renew request.

The Ledger DomainInbox accepts only tenant-scoped build/capability producers, so the platform-scoped catalog.policy_changed.v1 delivery stays pending. The producer records and retries it; the consumer extension is W05's write set and is not claimed here.
No workspace or Fabric caller consumes the plan/policy reads yet; those callers are W11/W15.
Administrator Console/BFF routes for the resource catalog product service are not wired (W13/W14/W23).
No production deployment, Candidate, publication or Instance qualification was performed, and no real provider resource was bought, charged or destroyed.
temporaryResources: Task-created loopback PostgreSQL container and anonymous volume removed; no production resource was accessed.
